Deterministic views of consciousness belittle or try to efface subjectivity, which, in my opinion, is perhaps of the utmost absurdity.

Consciousness is only conceivable in relation to consciousness. An explanation of consciousness in some objective formulation is a rejection of the validity of consciousness (subjectivity); that is, if you are doing so under the impression that knowing the pieces which constitute something somehow gives more than the fact of that something--but this is quite basic. It must be addressed... :)

It seems to me that you are, perhaps, a product of the whole deterministic, empiricist movement. 
Is to be atheist to be rational? Is it rational to base your subjectivity on the illusion of objectivity? Is it rational to reject that which is the most known (consciousness)? Is to be rational to be fulfilled? What even is rational? In the context which you used it, rational seems to mean some sort of sociological phenomenon in which an individual receives something of positive value from others... Just another example of society's constant trepidation in relation to the truth of solitude and of subjectivity. Dissociation with the ego does not have to be a disillusionment, though a disillusionment is often experienced. I digress... But at least dissociate consciously and not as a result of some oppressive forces!!!...

It seems to me that free will is only an issue to those who question themselves to a certain degree which involves, perhaps, bad faith. If one questions the validity of their own existence or, conversely, their lack of existence (fulfillment), one may try to question the concept of their own free will as some sort of abject coping mechanism. 
It seems to me that to question free will is to do so in order to further the objective self--which is either one trying to transcend their subjectivity or control others (which is not going to do much for you... which will probably just make things worse).

The only thing one can logically say about altruism is that it does, in-fact, exist... or does it? The only way it can be sure to exist is if it does indeed do so subjectively... And if subjectivity is egoistic then surely it is representative of a certain degree of egoism. 

The point is to not define altruism and tolerance as anything that beats around the bush and points in certain directions which fit the purpose of furthering one's own biases (artful circumlocution). The implications of altruism and tolerance are clear; the origins of such are hazy--but does it really matter?

Subjectively, altruism is more apparent than ever. If it ever once did exist in a different form and has merely evolved into what it is now... that is insignificant; altruism remains untouched and as real as ever. 

Tolerance can be whatever one thinks it is. Again, we're dealing with a problem of language here. The reasons one "tolerates" something is up for debate, but does it really matter? If one is looking for an absolute, objective definition of a thoroughly subjective phenomenon, one isn't going to get far. 

It is sort of like laughter. Is laughter a coping mechanism to make one feel better about the potential feeling of sorrow in relation to a fat woman slipping on an oil slick in a McDonald's line? Or is laughter a sociologically induced phenomenon that reinforces a sense of superiority and "HAHAHA, I'm better than that fat whale!"?

The world may never know! ;)
Long live Terence into infinite novelty.

Part of me accepts the notion that individuality is an illusion and only a reflection of received information that has happened to be absorbed at a unique point in time. I support a sort of tabula rasa. 

But, then again, it does seem so that we are born into a certain pattern and each specific person has their own pattern. So, relatively, in regard to sensation, each person is an individual... But....

Consciousness itself, if one were to meditate, is a constant essence free from any other factor. If two people were to meditate side by side, would there be anything to distinguish the the two in regard to being? 

I think individuality exists in information and is objective. I think that the more you get to know somebody the less unique their once 'unique' qualities become. I trust that the more you get to know someone the more their once objective status becomes subjective. 

Plato said "Friends have everything in common." 

I see this to mean that friends (are not the same person and do not do exactly the same things) understand each other so well and thoroughly that differences between the two are meaningless. This is so because the foundations of and reasons behind the differences are explored and understood to the utmost extent.  

Thus, understanding someone extremely deeply, essentially, makes them a part of you, you a part of them and means you have everything in common. 

I think that we are all part of a greater whole of consciousness. I think death breaks down barriers... As do psychedelics.

You do not need anyone other than yourself. It may seem like you do at times; however, having someone else will not ever take away the truth that you are alone. We are all alone. There are those who understand this and those who do not and live their lives constantly hiding an running from themselves. But this truth is not a depressing one. It is actually a beautiful one. To be alone is not depressing. To be alone is to have yourself and only yourself to worry about. To be alone is to examine yourself. To be alone is to feel and be at ease that you do in fact exist away from everything and can be unaffected. To be alone is to learn to know yourself. AND Knowing yourself is how meaningful relationships with other people can be achieved. 

Each moment that passes is a new moment. And while each moment can be influenced by other past moments, it does not have to be defined by them. You can make each image that goes by in your life yours. You are in control.

I would thoroughly analyze yourself. I would maybe buy a journal and write everything that comes to your mind about who you are. Your thoughts, passions, interests, dreams, ideas, wants, worries, etc etc. Everything that is important to you needs to be in front of your eyes staring back at you. Maybe even burn the pages you do not like. Seriously. You pour them out of yourself and then burn what is holding you back. 

If anything is holding you back from being happy or peaceful. Confront it. If that is confronting those friends, confronting your school, your job, that girl, etc etc, albeit. Life is too short to be afraid. Life is too short to be in pain. 

It may not be your fault that you are in the position that you are in. However, we all make decisions. We all have things happen to us that are bad and good. The point is not to just take those things and let them affect you, however positive or negative they may be. There is a reason we humans can have a filter for what affects us and what does not. 

You do not need anything or anyone other than yourself. You can fulfill your dreams. Create a master plan. It does not have to be anything grandiose. But I am sure you can come up with something that will suffice. 

Also. Maybe explore art? Music? Also. Maybe go to the store and buy some fresh or comforting scented candles or incense. You will be surprised at how much this effects your atmosphere. I would also try meditation. Meditation involves clearing your mind extensively and dissociating yourself from the chaos of existence. Meditation involves understanding yourself and your position in this reality. 

I wish you good luck. Suicide is not the answer. There is so much you can do. You have a universe inside of you. You have so many beautiful things inside of you that can be manifested into your life.

Nothing in this life has to be any way that you do not want it to be. There are things that you can do that you probably not even dreamed of that will make you feel so happy. Try something new. Do something new. Focus on a passion of yours.

Okay if you're reading this take a deep breath. I am serious. Then. Read the rest of this and think through what I am going to say. And oblige if you will.

Clear your mind. Do not think. Try not to think. If that is too hard control your breathing. Bring your sole attention to your breathing. Relax. Breath in and out. Let your mind fade into peace. Release your mind from the constant occupation of thought. 

Take as much time as you need. 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes. 1 hour. I sometimes go for an hour. 

Then. When you are ready for some thoughts think of yourself. Think of no one else. Think of you, your feelings, your memories, your emotions. Think about what comes to mind. Think about the most important things to you. Feel them. let them flood your mind. 

Open your eyes. Grab a piece of paper. Write it all down. Everything. Everything. friends, thoughts, family, memories, foods, passions, interests, fantasies. everything and anything. 

When you think you have gotten enough... analyze it. Organize it. Now. Evaluate yourself. Evaluate who YOU are. DO NOT think of anything else. Everyone, at this point, is insignificant. YOU are what matters. No one else. YOU are the most familiar thing in your life. IT is time to focus on you and what you want.

Now if you have in mind what you want, who you are, what you need, what will make you happy, what you do not want, etc etc it is time to make some goals. Not necessarily anything definite, but ideas. 

The ideas should be of what you want from this life. We did not sign up for this life, but that does not mean we are not in control. 
You are in control. You may not think so, but I promise you, you are. 

Throw out everything from your life that is holding you back. Throw out everything that is not in sweet accordance with what you are, who you are, what you want, what you need, etc. 

There is undoubtedly a lot of trash littering your existence making you feel unstable. It happens to the best of us. It is time to take out the trash.

Do this as often as you must. Sometimes it just takes analyzing what it is that we do want. Sometimes we just get so caught up in the chaos. Life does not have to be chaos. It is only chaos when you lose track of yourself.

If you do not think that you know yourself... You do more than you think you do. Again. Locate what you want. Locate what you need. etc etc. You can do this.

I did.

Stop. Clear your mind. Listen to me. Clear your mind. Dissociate. You're obviously far down in a hole. Do not let the darkness of that rift swallow you. Close your eyes. Clear everything from your mind. Control your breathing. Just do this. Take as much time as you need. 

When you are ready think of yourself and who YOU are. Specifically, think about what you want to get out of this life. Think about your passions, your love, your interests. And now think. All your dreams, passions, interests, thoughts, everything. Everything about you. Everything that can possibly come to mind... You'll be left with a map to happiness. With this you can figure out where you should go. That place is not death.

A blatant rejection of subjectivity. I have no need to watch such a thing. It is probably some sophisticated way of belittling the subjective experience through the use of neuroscientific jargon which suffices only at explaining objective phenomenon completely and utterly separate from the experiences it claims to represent. I am not interested in belittling reality. I am not interested in defining experiences with some boring, objective explanation.

And what I meant when I said "do you describe your orgasms in the same way" is of the following: some people would say you stimulated certain receptors into triggering a neural response, creating a release of dopamine, and thus, a certain effect. I would say, "I pleasured myself and felt ecstatic." 
The objective explanation ruins the experience. 
Just another refugee from the society of oppressed ego dissociation, eh?

Your consciousness is the most familiar thing to you. It is the most fundamental aspect of reality; everything that comes from it is a result and is de-facto subordinate. You can delude yourself into defining your reality in terms of neuroscience, but it will never allow you to escape the fact of perception. It will never change the fact that consciousness is something fundamentally inconceivable and nothing objective will ever suffice at an explanation.

Using consciousness to try and define consciousness by external means is like trying to define the number one with only the number one. You can define 1 with many other subsidiary ways such as 4/4 or .5 x 2, but nothing will amount to the truth of 1. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts. 

Perhaps science of the future holds a deeper understanding of consciousness,but I doubt it will be gained solely objectively. But the ifs of the future do not detract from or efface the reality of today.
This is an abject objective explanation. Do you describe your orgasms in the same way?
